Maria (sec): Heads up — customer reported admin sessions in Private control plane sometimes lose elevated perms after a couple minutes. Seems tied to rolling LB -> different node.
Ken (eng-runtime): ugh. session affinity + RBAC token binding? any repro steps?
Maria (sec): They said: login via bastion -> open console -> can create rolebinding -> after ~2m actions start 403'ing.
Oliver (onprem): I saw similar pattern in staging last week after the role-refactor. Could be session store not carrying the bound role claim across backends.
Jamie (sre): Can you paste a failing request log? I only have coarse kube-audit entries.
Maria (sec): Pasted minimal trace from customer (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/admin/roles 403 denied user="svcacct-cp" reason="missing_permission:create_role" node=controlplane-2
```

Ken (eng-runtime): svcacct-cp should have impersonation to create rolebindings. Maybe KMS-wrapped tokens are being reissued without the role alias. We changed encryption context in the refactor.
Oliver (onprem): That rings true. Onprem private control plane uses KMS to seal session tokens with context: `deployment=private,env=prod`. If one node uses `deployment=private,env=prod` and another still has old context `deploy=private`, the unseal will succeed but without metadata -> token drops role claim.
Jamie (sre): How are audit logs showing these events? audit-bot: Missing explicit audit entry for token-unseal-failure; only the resultant 403 is logged.
Maria (sec): Customer also noticed gaps in audit logs around the moment of denial — no KMS errors.
Ken (eng-runtime): Possible silent fallback path in our token unseal code: on KMS context mismatch we still return minimal session (no role claims) instead of failing hard. That preserves availability but loses authorization.
Oliver (onprem): Repro recipe I used: 1) create session on controlplane-1 2) create a canary role 3) trigger LB switch to controlplane-2 4) attempt privileged action -> 403.
Ken (eng-runtime): Thanks. I can repro locally. Confirmed logs: `unseal: context_mismatch=true; returning guest_session`
Maria (sec): This is severity P1 for Private/Dedicated customers — breaks least privilege guarantees.
Jamie (sre): Quick mitigation: add a short-lived rule in LB to sticky sessions for 10m until we patch? Might be easy for dedicated customers.
Oliver (onprem): Sticky sessions buy time but doesn't fix node config drift. We should also detect and alert when unseal returns stripped session.
Ken (eng-runtime): I propose the following immediate actions:
- Make unseal fail hard on context mismatch (will cause auth errors but clear signal).
- Add audit log entry `token_unseal_context_mismatch` with node id and session id.
- Roll a coordinated config sync to enforce consistent KMS context across nodes.
Maria (sec): +1. Also we need an incident advisory template for affected customers.
Jamie (sre): I'll open infra alert: `KMS_CONTEXT_MISMATCH_RATE` and add pager if > 0 for prod-private clusters.
Ken (eng-runtime): Patch PR incoming: `reject on context mismatch` + new audit entry. Will run canary on staging.
Oliver (onprem): For on-prem kit customers we need a KB: "KMS context upgrade checklist" — include `kubectl get nodes` config check and rolling restart guidance.
Maria (sec): Also add an evaluation to the RBAC rollout playbook: detect silent-drop of role claims in session tokens.
Jamie (sre): Action items assigned: Ken -> PR + rollout plan. Oliver -> KB + onprem notice. Maria -> customer advisory + postmortem skeleton. I will create the alert and dashboard.
Ken (eng-runtime): PR: https://phabricator.redwood/XXXXX (wip)
Maria (sec): Good. One more ask — can we surface affected sessions to customers via console (session ID list) so they can revoke if needed? Not required for fix but good for trust.
Oliver (onprem): That requires audit log enrichment. Add to backlog.
Jamie (sre): I'll set last_message_ts to track follow-ups. For now triage status: INVESTIGATING. :eyes:
audit-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-542 (auto)"
